name: Massachusetts
kicker: The Bay State · Pilgrims, Puritans, and the first shots of the Revolution
briefing: Massachusetts is where the Pilgrims landed in 1620, where Puritans founded Boston ten years later, and where the first shots of the American Revolution were fired at Lexington and Concord. It officially calls itself a commonwealth, and four presidents were born there, including John Adams and John F. Kennedy. Basketball and volleyball were both invented there, too.
answerHtml: Massachusetts (accept Commonwealth of Massachusetts or Massachusetts Bay Colony; prompt on Massachusetts Bay Company)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: William Bradford served as governor of a colony in this future state for about thirty years and wrote a history of its founding. Before going ashore in 1620, 41 men of that colony signed an agreement to make “just and equal laws.”
tossups.r: Squanto helped those Pilgrims survive after they arrived on the _Mayflower_. For 10 points, name this New England state, home to Plymouth Rock.

tossups.p: In a 1630 sermon, John Winthrop told the Puritans sailing with him on the _Arbella_ [“ar-BELL-uh”] that their new colony would be “a city upon a hill,” watched by the eyes of all people. Winthrop’s colonists soon founded the town that became this state’s capital.
tossups.r: Winthrop served as that colony’s governor many times. For 10 points, name this New England state, whose capital is Boston.

tossups.p: Anne Hutchinson was put on trial and banished from this colony after she held meetings to discuss sermons and claimed to receive messages directly from God. In 1636, Roger Williams had fled this colony and founded Providence.
tossups.r: Both exiles settled in what became Rhode Island. For 10 points, name this “Bay State,” where Puritans founded a colony around Boston.

tossups.p: A 1647 law in this colony, nicknamed the “Old Deluder Satan Act,” required towns with at least 50 families to hire a teacher so children could learn to read the Bible. This colony’s legislature had also founded the oldest college in the United States in 1636.
tossups.r: That college, Harvard, is in Cambridge, across the Charles River from Boston. For 10 points, name this New England state.

tossups.p: Mary Rowlandson wrote a best-selling account of the months she spent as a captive after Native warriors raided her town of Lancaster in this colony in 1676. That raid came during a war led by Metacom, a Wampanoag [“wahm-puh-NOH-ag”] leader whom the English called King Philip.
tossups.r: Metacom was the son of Massasoit, who had helped the Pilgrims. For 10 points, name this New England state, where the Pilgrims had landed at Plymouth.

tossups.p: Tituba, an enslaved woman, was one of the first people accused during a 1692 panic in this colony, and Cotton Mather later wrote a book defending the trials that followed. Arthur Miller’s play _The Crucible_ retells those events, in which about 20 people were put to death.
tossups.r: Nathaniel Hawthorne, who was born in the town where those trials took place, set _The Scarlet Letter_ in this colony. For 10 points, name this state, home to the town of Salem.

tossups.p: In 1774, Parliament closed this colony’s main port until its people paid for destroyed tea, and it took away much of this colony’s power to govern itself. General Thomas Gage became this colony’s governor to enforce those Coercive Acts.
tossups.r: Colonists called those laws the Intolerable Acts. For 10 points, name this colony, where the Boston Tea Party took place.

tossups.p: Ralph Waldo Emerson’s “Concord Hymn” honors the farmers of this state who “fired the shot heard round the world” at a bridge in April 1775. On the night before that fight, Paul Revere and William Dawes rode out to warn that British troops were coming.
tossups.r: Those first battles of the Revolution were at Lexington and Concord. For 10 points, name this state, which honors them every April on Patriots’ Day.

tossups.p: Henry Knox hauled cannons from Fort Ticonderoga to Dorchester Heights, forcing British troops to leave this state’s capital on March 17, 1776. The year before, the British had won a costly victory nearby at Breed’s Hill, in a battle usually named for a different hill.
tossups.r: That battle was Bunker Hill. For 10 points, name this state, where the Revolution began at Lexington and Concord.

tossups.p: Elizabeth Freeman, known as Mum Bett, won her freedom in 1781 by suing under this state’s new constitution, which said that “all men are born free and equal.” After the Quock Walker cases, this state’s highest court ruled that slavery could not exist under that constitution.
tossups.r: John Adams wrote most of that constitution, the oldest written constitution still in use. For 10 points, name this New England state.

tossups.p: Governor James Bowdoin [“BOH-din”] sent a militia under General Benjamin Lincoln to put down a revolt by farmers deep in debt in the western part of this state. In 1787, those farmers failed to capture the federal arsenal at Springfield.
tossups.r: That revolt, led by Daniel Shays, convinced many leaders to write a stronger constitution. For 10 points, name this state where four presidents, including both Adamses, were born.

tossups.p: A carved wooden fish called the “Sacred Cod” hangs in the chamber of this state’s House of Representatives. William King, who became Maine’s first governor, led the movement for Maine to separate from this state, which finally happened in 1820 under the Missouri Compromise.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this New England state, home to Cape Cod and the islands of Nantucket and Martha’s Vineyard.

tossups.p: Young women who worked in this state’s textile mills wrote and published their own magazine, _The Lowell Offering_. Those mills, built by the Boston Associates, stood in a town named for Francis Cabot Lowell, who had memorized the designs of British power looms.
tossups.r: Those workers were called the Lowell mill girls. For 10 points, name this state, an early center of the Industrial Revolution in America.

tossups.p: William Lloyd Garrison began publishing his antislavery newspaper, _The Liberator_, in this state’s capital in 1831. During the Civil War, Robert Gould Shaw led this state’s 54th Regiment, one of the first official Black units in the Union Army, in an attack on Fort Wagner.
tossups.r: The 1989 film _Glory_ tells that regiment’s story. For 10 points, name this state, whose senator Charles Sumner fought slavery in Congress.

tossups.p: James Naismith invented basketball at a YMCA school in Springfield in this state in 1891, and William Morgan invented volleyball a few years later in nearby Holyoke. The first subway in the United States opened under the streets of this state’s capital in 1897.
tossups.r: That capital also hosts the Boston Marathon. For 10 points, name this state where John Adams and John F. Kennedy were born.

clues.t: Capital and largest city: Boston
The Pilgrims landed at Plymouth in 1620 aboard the _Mayflower_
The Revolution began at Lexington and Concord (April 19, 1775), remembered on Patriots’ Day
Nicknamed the Bay State; officially called a commonwealth
Birthplace of four presidents: John Adams, John Quincy Adams, John F. Kennedy, and George H. W. Bush
John Winthrop led the Puritans of the Bay Colony and called it “a city upon a hill” (1630)
After the Boston Tea Party (1773), Parliament’s Coercive (Intolerable) Acts closed Boston’s port, and General Thomas Gage became governor
Salem witch trials (1692): about 20 people were put to death; retold in Arthur Miller’s _The Crucible_
Harvard (1636), the oldest college in the United States, is in Cambridge
Shays’ Rebellion (1786–1787): farmers in the western part of the state rose up over debts and taxes
Maine was part of it until 1820, when Maine became a free state in the Missouri Compromise
Basketball (Springfield, 1891) and volleyball (Holyoke, 1895) were invented there; the first U.S. subway opened in Boston (1897)
Geography: Cape Cod and the islands of Nantucket and Martha’s Vineyard
William Bradford governed Plymouth for about thirty years; 41 men signed the Mayflower Compact (1620) before going ashore
It banished Roger Williams, who founded Providence (1636), and Anne Hutchinson; both settled in what became Rhode Island
The “Old Deluder Satan Act” (1647) made towns of 50 families hire a teacher
King Philip’s War (1675–1676), led by Metacom (son of Massasoit); Mary Rowlandson wrote about her captivity
Tituba was among the first accused at Salem; Cotton Mather wrote a book defending the trials
Emerson’s “Concord Hymn”: “the shot heard round the world”; Paul Revere and William Dawes rode to warn of the British
Henry Knox brought cannons from Fort Ticonderoga to Dorchester Heights, and the British left Boston (March 17, 1776); Bunker Hill was fought mostly on Breed’s Hill
Elizabeth Freeman (Mum Bett) won her freedom in court (1781); after the Quock Walker cases, slavery ended there
Its 1780 constitution, written mostly by John Adams, is the oldest written constitution still in use
Governor James Bowdoin sent General Benjamin Lincoln to stop Shays’ Rebellion; the rebels failed to take the Springfield arsenal (1787)
Lowell mill girls published _The Lowell Offering_; Francis Cabot Lowell had memorized British loom designs
William Lloyd Garrison’s _The Liberator_ (Boston, 1831); Robert Gould Shaw led the 54th Regiment (the film _Glory_)
A wooden “Sacred Cod” hangs in its House chamber; William King led Maine’s split and became Maine’s first governor
Nathaniel Hawthorne, born in Salem, set _The Scarlet Letter_ in Puritan Boston

trap.title: Colony, city, or state?
trap.body: Massachusetts tossups use clues about places inside it that have their own answer lines: Boston (its capital), Plymouth Colony (the Pilgrims’ separate colony, which joined Massachusetts in 1691), Salem, and Cape Cod. Maine was also part of Massachusetts until 1820, so early Maine history can turn up in a Massachusetts question. Answering with the city or the colony when the question wants the state loses the tossup.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “this city” is Boston, and “this colony founded by the Pilgrims” is Plymouth Colony. “This state” or “this commonwealth” is Massachusetts, and a question about John Winthrop’s Puritan colony takes Massachusetts Bay Colony or just Massachusetts.
trap.line: Real answer line: Massachusetts (accept Commonwealth of Massachusetts or Massachusetts Bay Colony)
